Visitor Overview: native construction grammar (source extraction)

Images read: native-pe-images.json reference and classic, DF 53.16.
The classic source identity is PE:6a70b91c:0270a000.
Classic owner: 0x1401a5b00..0x1401a8679.
Visitor construction: 0x1401a6320..0x1401a6a6f.
This file records source semantics, not a test or a game-observation report.

The source is assembled once, then passed to curses_text_boxst::add_paragraph
(classic 0x1408e4b80) with width 28 at 0x1401a6a6a. Physical English line
breaks do not identify independent sentences or independent translation keys.

State and itinerary pseudocode
-----------------------------
if unit.travel_log == null:
    do not create this visitor paragraph
if the existing overview paragraph vector is nonempty:
    do not construct the visitor paragraph again in this branch

if travel_log.flags & 4:                       # WANT_TO_LEAVE
    source = "This visitor is ready to leave."
else if not (travel_log.flags & 1):             # CHATTED_WITH_LOCAL
    source = "You can learn more about this visitor after they chat with a local."
else:
    source = "This visitor has come "
    remaining = travel_log.itinerary.size
    for entry in travel_log.itinerary:          # original vector order
        switch entry.type:
            0:  source += "to pray"
            1:  source += "to study"
            2:  source += "to relax"
            3:  source += "to perform"
            4:  source += "to slay beasts"
            5:  source += "seeking work as a performer"
            6:  source += "seeking work as a mercenary"
            7:  source += "seeking work as a scholar"
            8:  source += "for diplomacy"
            9:  source += "seeking sanctuary"
            10: source += "asking questions"
            default: append no purpose literal

        if entry.site_id != -1 and entry.location_id != -1:
            site = find_site(entry.site_id)
            location = site ? find_abstract_building(site, entry.location_id) : null
            language_name = location ? location.virtual(+0x10)() : null
            if language_name != null:
                source += " at "
                source += format_language_name(language_name, capitalized=true,
                                               last_option=false)

        if remaining >= 3: source += ", "
        else if remaining == 2: source += " and "
        remaining -= 1
    source += "."

    if travel_log.original_reason != -1:
        destination = ""
        if travel_log.original_goal_ab_id != -1:
            site = find_site(current_site_id)
            location = site ? find_abstract_building(site,
                              travel_log.original_goal_ab_id) : null
            language_name = location ? location.virtual(+0x10)() : null
            if language_name != null:
                destination = format_language_name(language_name,
                               capitalized=true, last_option=false)
        source += "  "
        source += personal_pronoun(unit.sex, capitalized=true)
        source += " "
        source += rumor_clause(travel_log.original_reason, destination, unit)

The two-space sentence separator is native authored whitespace. A missing
destination lookup, null language-name pointer, or empty rendered name selects
the literal "this" branch for the clauses below. It is not an unnamed place
type. Each itinerary item independently has its optional " at NAME" suffix.
The itinerary count, repeated types, and combinations are dynamic source data;
there is no single-purpose-only restriction in this constructor.

Rumor-clause pseudocode
----------------------
place = destination != "" ? destination : "this"
switch original_reason:
    41: return "heard this was a good place to search for monsters."
    42: return "heard " + place + " was the place to entertain people."
    44: return "heard " + place + " was the place to perform research."
    54: if destination == "":
            return "went on this journey out of curiosity."
        return "was curious about " + destination + "."
    55: return "heard " + place + " would make a good base for a mercenary."
    56: return "heard " + place + " was the place to look for long-term work."
    57: return "heard " + place + " was the place for long-term scholarship."
    58: return "heard " + place + " was the place for a good drink."
    59: return "heard " + place + " was the place to admire fine architecture."
    60: return "heard " + place + " was the place for prayer."
    61: return "heard " + place + " was the place to enjoy oneself."
    62: return "heard this was the place for those seeking danger."
    74: clause = "is seeking information"
        if unit.current_action != null and unit.current_action.type == 17:
            artifact_id = first_int32(unit.current_action.data)
            clause += " about the location of "
            clause += format_artifact_name(artifact_id, mode=0)
        return clause + "."
    75: return "believes " + place + " would be a safe place to stay."
    default: return ""

The switch addresses and all values 41..75 are retained in
classic-native-branches.tsv. The default branch is also selected by values
outside that range. No source period is appended by the default rumor branch:
the previously appended capitalized pronoun and trailing space remain in the
source. original_reason == -1 skips the complete second-sentence prefix.
An empty itinerary vector produces the literal source
"This visitor has come ." before any optional rumor text. An unknown itinerary
type appends no purpose literal but can still append a location and a list
separator. These are native fallthrough semantics, not invented purpose names.

Personal pronoun helper
-----------------------
Classic 0x140aa17b0..0x140aa1824 (full source in classic-pronoun-helper.asm).
sex == 1: "he"; sex == 0: "she"; otherwise: "it".
The visitor call at 0x1401a6664 uses capitalized=true, producing He/She/It.
The helper has no additional pronoun or plural branch.

Artifact-name helper and all fallback fields
-------------------------------------------
Classic 0x140b91440..0x140b91750; reference 0x140b94400.
The visitor call at 0x1401a6a1e passes r9d=0. The helper's only mode bit
used here is bit 2 (mode & 2), which creates Legends link markup. Mode 0
therefore creates plain visible field text and cannot produce LPAGE markup.

function format_artifact_name(id, mode):
    artifact = binary_find(world.artifacts, id)
    if artifact == null or id == -1:
        return "an unknown artifact"
    item = artifact.item                        # artifact + 0x90
    is_book_kind() = item.type == 89 or item.type == 87 or item.has_tool_use(20)
    # Native predicates run lazily; named plain output need not dereference
    # the item. Link mode runs these predicates before the name formatter.
    if mode & 2:
        output += is_book_kind() ? "[LPAGE:BOOK:" : "[LPAGE:ARTIFACT:"
        output += decimal(artifact.id) + "]"
    name = format_language_name(artifact.name, capitalized=true,
                                last_option=false)
    if name != "":
        output += name
    else if is_book_kind():
        output += "Untitled"
    else:
        output += item_identity(item, ignore_artifact=false, article_mode=1)
    if mode & 2:
        output += "[/LPAGE]"
    return output

"Untitled" is assembled by immediate integer stores of
0x64656c7469746e55 at 0x140b915f0 and 0x140b9164b, then an explicit NUL.
It is therefore not found by a RIP-relative literal-only inventory.
The book-kind conditions are native type 89 (book), type 87 (slab), or the
item virtual +0xe0 tool-use predicate with value 20. A successful named
language field is retained even for those kinds; empty book names use Untitled.
The name formatter handles generated language word forms, authored first
names/nicknames, The/the and of/Of structure. It supplies capitalization for
the artifact language name; it does not capitalize the ordinary item fallback.

The item fallback is classic 0x140c62490..0x140c62f4a, reference 0x140c65450.
It spans consecutive unwind records split at 0x140c6275d; the complete
continuation is in classic-artifact-item-fallback.asm.
Its arguments in this constructor are ignore_artifact=false and article_mode=1.
It first honors an artifact-reference language name when present. If the
record has no rendered name, it enters the native quality/count/identity
formatter, including item virtual +0x5f0 (article) and +0x5e8 (complete noun).
The same item-identity helper also has a title-copy production before that
noun path: when ignore_artifact=false, a book item's nonempty stored title,
or a tool's first nonempty written-content title reached through improvement
kind 12 (writing) or kind 9 (pages), produces TITLE + " (copy)". The outer
artifact helper's book-kind branches intercept ordinary books and tools
with use 20 before this fallback, but the item helper retains that production
for other written tools. This is an article-free written title field, not a
material/type phrase. The suffix is at 0x140c62734 and remains literal syntax.

The ordinary article helper is classic 0x140c62420..0x140c62485, reference
0x140c653e0. It returns lowercase "the " for article_mode==1. For mode 0 it
returns "a " only for non-artifact items of quantity 1; other modes omit the
article. Consequently the ordinary unnamed visitor fallback begins "the ",
even though a generated named artifact can begin uppercase "The ".

Body-component/corpse/corpse-piece classes override article formatting at
classic 0x140c9dda0..0x140c9de84, reference 0x140ca0d60. A named associated
historical figure/unit, or the current named adventure figure, suppresses
the article; otherwise the same mode 1 "the "/mode 0 "a " cases apply.
The following typed noun formatter owns that whole corpse/body identity.

After the article, the item fallback retains its actual typed item name,
material/species components, quantities, pair/plural variants, description
subjects, and quality/wear/improvement/state/magic designation characters.
Its native semantic noun inventory is already recorded in
data/extracted/item-description-sources.tsv and item-info-title-sources.tsv,
including all 98 RTTI owners and the title/article slots. This field must
resolve through that complete item grammar before a broad generated-name
fallback is allowed to consume ordinary item nouns. It is not a finite
list of observed artifact names and is not the full multi-sentence item
description constructor at reference 0x140c75000.

Saved local helper source files
------------------------------
classic-pronoun-helper.asm / classic-pronoun-helper-literals.tsv
classic-artifact-name-helper.asm / classic-artifact-name-helper-literals.tsv

classic-item-article-helper.asm

Additional paragraph in the SAME visitor text cell: prophet quotation
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Source image: classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000
Outer construction: classic 0x1401a6a6f..0x1401a6bc5;
reference Steam 0x1401a6adf..0x1401a6c35.
Mental-picture formatter: classic 0x140656ab0..0x1406579ad executable
instructions, embedded switch tables through unwind end 0x140657c70;
reference Steam entry 0x140659090.
Subject/object formatter: classic 0x140656840..0x140656aaa.
Profession enum 0x83 is PROPHET, from df.d_basics.xml / native profession
source inventory; it is not HUNTER. The quotation is an additional paragraph
in the visitor overview cell, rather than the bottom personality quote.

if (unit.travel_log.flags & 1) && unit.profession == 0x83:
    belief_id = unit_belief_id(unit)                 // 0x1413f48f0
    if belief_id == -1: stop additional-paragraph branch
    belief = find_by_id(world.belief_systems.all, belief_id) // 0x140072500
    if belief == null || belief.story.empty(): stop
    story = belief.story[random_index(belief.story.size())]
    if story.story_frame.empty(): stop
    frame_index = random_index(story.story_frame.size())
    if frame_index == -1: stop
    actor_context = { -1, unit.hist_figure_id }     // stack +0x50/+0x54
    listener_context = { -1, -1 }                  // stack +0x40/+0x44
    body = format_picture(story.story_frame[frame_index].mental_picture,
                          actor_context, listener_context)
    add_line(owner + 0x1970, "")                    // native blank spacer
    add_paragraph(owner + 0x1970, '"' + body + '"', width=28)

unit_belief_id first consults the historical figure's current identity via
0x1413adfa0; if its identity.belief_system at +0x9c is not -1, return it.
Otherwise collect up to the first ten IDs from the figure's
knowledge/religious_data.belief_system_id list. No entries returns -1;
otherwise select one ID (randomly if more than one). This can return -1
and therefore prevent the extra quotation. Selection of a story/frame is
random each time this source is constructed. Frame.relation and its related
frame index are not formatted or recursively followed by this helper.

format_picture(picture, actor_context, listener_context):
    output = ""
    time = first property with virtual getType() == 8  // TIME
    action = first property with getType() == 1         // ACTION
    if action exists:
        if action.actor_element == -1: return ""
        subject = picture.elements[action.actor_element]
        output += format_element(subject, grammar_role=0)
        output += " "
        first_person = subject.type == HF && subject.hf == actor_context.hf
        second_person = !first_person && subject.type == HF &&
                        subject.hf == listener_context.hf
        past = time != null && (time.spec_flag & 1)
        future = time != null && (time.spec_flag & 2)
        continuous = action.spec_flag & 1
        if continuous:
            if time != null:
                if past: output += (second_person ? "were " : "was ")
                if future: output += "will be "
                // Existing TIME with no flags adds NO present copula.
                // Both flags add both past and future strings in this order.
            else:
                output += first_person ? "am " : second_person ? "are " : "is "
        else if future:
            output += "will "
        switch action.action:
            0 APPEAR:  forms = { appear, appears, appeared, appearing }
            1 DESTROY: forms = { destroy, destroys, destroyed, destroying }
            2 SPOKE:   forms = { speak, speaks, spoke, speaking }
            3 BURN:    forms = { burn, burns, burned, burning }
            4 FLOOD:   forms = { flood, floods, flooded, flooding }
            5 REWARD:  forms = { reward, rewards, rewarded, rewarding }
            default:   forms = empty; append NO verb
        if forms not empty:
            if continuous: append forms.continuous
            else if past: append forms.past
            else if future || first_person || second_person: append forms.base
            else: append forms.third_person
        if action.target_element != -1:
            output += " "
            if action.action == 2: output += "to "
            output += format_element(picture.elements[action.target_element],1)
        output += "."
        return output

    emotion = first property with getType() == 3        // EMOTION
    if emotion exists:
        if emotion.element == -1: return ""
        subject = picture.elements[emotion.element]
        output += format_element(subject, grammar_role=0)
        output += " "
        first_person / second_person as above
        if time != null && (time.spec_flag & 1):
            output += second_person ? "were " : "was "
        else if time != null && (time.spec_flag & 2):
            output += "will be "
        else:
            output += first_person ? "am " : second_person ? "are " : "is "
        output += emotion_switch(emotion.emotion)
        output += "."
        return output

    // DATE, TOOL, COLOR_PATTERN, SHAPE, ADJECTIVE and POSITION properties
    // do not produce any text through this helper. No subject fallback.
    capitalize_first_letter(output)                  // 0x14052b070
    return output                                   // still empty

The native action and emotion switch are not transitive/passive inference:
the formatter literally selects the six verb forms and the subject/object
from separate indexed elements. All temporal flag branches above follow
the binary, including TIME with flags=0, TIME with both bits, unrecognized
action values, and unrecognized emotion values. A subject element of an
unrecognized type contributes an empty string, but following spaces, verbs,
copulas, targets and punctuation still survive.

The complete indexed emotion switch (-1..168, 170 table entries) is saved
in classic-prophet-emotion-branches.tsv. It records enum numeric value,
upstream enum name, native case address, native string address, and literal.
-1 (ANYTHING) emits "emotionless". Empty literal rows jump to 0x140657980:
no adjective/emotion is appended, but the already-appended subject/copula
and final period remain. Values outside [-1,168] do the same. Thus a native
source such as "I am ." is a real default production, not a missing capture.
All static helper references are preserved in
classic-visitor-extra-quote-helper-literals.tsv; action forms and each
object separator are in classic-prophet-action-branches.tsv.

format_element(element, grammar_role):
    // This helper APPENDS to its caller's string.
    switch element.getType():
        0 HF:
            if element.hf == actor_context.hf:
                0 -> "I"; 1 -> "me"; 2 -> "my"; 3 -> "myself"
                other role -> empty
            else if element.hf == listener_context.hf:
                0 or 1 -> "you"; 2 -> "your"; 3 -> "yourself"
                other role -> empty
            else:
                context = init_hf_name_context()     // 0x140072010
                // flags=0, pointers=null, all subject/object IDs=-1
                format_hf_name(world.history.figures, element.hf, context,
                               grammar_role=0, descriptor_mode=1)
                               // 0x140b8ff50
        1 SITE:
            format_site_name(world.world_data, element.site, mode=0)
                               // 0x140b90970
        2 REGION:
            // Deliberately ignores element.region: source uses world's name.
            language_name(world.world_data.name, capitalize=true, native=false)
                               // 0x140a91760
        other type:
            append empty

In THIS outer paragraph actor_context.hf is the visitor's historical-figure
ID and listener_context.hf is -1. Normally this produces first-person I/me
or actual historical-figure/site/world names; the raw helper still has a
"you" branch for an element ID of -1. The sentence constructor calls role
0 for subjects and role 1 for action targets. At classic 0x140656f09
(reference 0x1406594e9) mov r12d,1 explicitly overwrites the earlier
first-person boolean before r12w is stored as the object grammar role.
Consequently an action object naming the speaker is "me", never "I".
It never calls possessive or reflexive roles (2,3), although their literal
branches are saved as source.
Neither subject formatter nor sentence formatter capitalizes a lowercase
unnamed/unknown subject after successful action/emotion construction.

Reachable historical-figure name branches under the initialized context
and descriptor_mode=1:
    no figure with this ID -> "an unknown creature"
    figure has a language_name -> capitalized generated historical-figure name
    figure has NO language_name ->
        "a " + optional "zombie " + optional "ghostly " +
        creature/caste singular name + optional " " + interaction_profile.name
The generic helper's named-figure species/undead prefixes are disabled by
descriptor_mode=1. Unnamed figures still retain those typed prefixes.
Caste-singular naming at 0x140aa0c50 uses caste singular name if valid and
nonempty, otherwise creature singular name; invalid race can be empty.
No hardcoded replacement such as "creature" is inserted by that helper.
The helper receives plural=false and the historical figure's race and caste.
These are semantic creature nouns, not proper names.
The prefix "zombie " depends on interaction_profile.undead_name at +0x150
being nonempty (its string length is at +0x160). The appended final display
name is a DIFFERENT field: interaction_profile.use_display_name at +0x88
requests " " + interaction_profile.name at +0x90. This spacer is appended
even if that display-name string is empty. The "ghostly " prefix depends
on the first historical-figure flag byte having bit 0x80 and
use_display_name being false; it is not combined with a display-name suffix.
Thus all reachable suffixes use the existing native interaction display-name
semantics. src/creature_descriptors.inc recognizes the full known display
name after a complete species (including generated species) and handles
the preceding zombie/ghostly prefixes. Those display-name families are
already extracted from CE_DISPLAY_NAME and the resurrection/ghoul/ghost/
mummy adjective+noun native generator tables by
tools/build_creature_vocabulary.py. They do not need a broad personal-name
fallback to consume their semantic nouns.

The generic HF formatter also contains context-dependent "interrogator",
"subject", "Nameless", "an unidentified creature", article "the ",
possessive "'s", additional name + " the " + species/undead description,
and [LPAGE:HF:ID] markup branches. The mental-picture caller's initialized
context/role0/descriptor_mode1 make those branches unreachable in this
visitor paragraph. Their complete native instructions and literal refs are
saved to preserve the original helper rather than omit them as source.

Reachable site helper mode0:
    no site with this ID -> "an unknown site"
    site exists -> capitalized generated site language_name (possibly empty)
The helper's LPAGE:SITE markup mode is not requested by this caller.
The REGION case directly formats world_data.name at structure offset0:
this is confirmed by df.region.xml's world_data.name definition (world name).
It does not format a subregion's geographic name or an entity name.
